lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.name: Vietnamese Chicken Hot Pot with Bird’s-Eye Chili
aliases: Chicken hot pot with bird’s-eye chili
lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.serving_basis: One shared hot pot for four people.
lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.description: Free-range chicken simmers with lotus seeds, lotus root, shiitake mushrooms and coconut water; bird’s-eye chili brings gentle heat that diners can adjust at the table. Bếp Việt edits the seasoning for a family meal while retaining the defining ingredients of this chicken hot pot.
lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.finished_dish: The broth is fragrant and gently sweet from the chicken and coconut water; the lotus seeds are tender, the lotus root retains a little bite and the chicken is fully cooked and soft.
lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.serving: Set the hot pot in the middle of the table and serve with greens and fresh rice noodles. Keep extra chilies on the side so each diner can choose the heat level.
tips: Soak the shiitake mushrooms and lotus seeds ahead of time; skim the broth when it first boils for a clearer soup.
Add bird’s-eye chilies gradually and taste before adding more; leave them whole for milder heat.
Cook the chicken fully near the bone and use separate utensils for raw poultry and ready-to-eat greens.

lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.image_alt: A Vietnamese chicken hot pot with free-range chicken, lotus seeds, lotus root, mushrooms and red chilies, isolated on a transparent background.
lau-ga-tiem-ot-hiem.time_note: About 155 minutes including soaking and marinating; simmering time varies with the size of the chicken pieces.

preparation_steps: Rinse and pat dry the chicken, then marinate with some of the fish sauce and salt for about 20 minutes. Handle raw chicken separately from greens and ready-to-eat ingredients.

Soak the lotus seeds and shiitake mushrooms until tender, then strain any soaking liquid to remove grit. Peel and slice the lotus root; bruise the lemongrass and shallots, and rinse the chilies, jujubes and goji berries.
Trim and wash the greens, then drain. Prepare the rice noodles and hot-pot burner.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sear the chicken in batches until the exterior is lightly browned; transfer to a clean plate.
Sauté the shallots and lemongrass until fragrant. Add coconut water, stock, lotus root, lotus seeds, jujubes and mushrooms. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add the chicken and simmer gently for about 60–75 minutes until fully cooked and tender. Season with the remaining fish sauce, salt and rock sugar; add the goji berries during the final 10 minutes.
Move the pot to the table burner and adjust the chili heat. Briefly cook the greens in the broth and serve with rice noodles.

ga-ac-tiem-thuoc-bac.name: Black Silkie Chicken Steamed with Chinese Herbs
ga-ac-tiem-thuoc-bac.serving_basis: Two small individual pots, with about half a chicken or a portion of broth per diner.
ga-ac-tiem-thuoc-bac.description: Black silkie chicken is lightly seasoned and steamed in covered pots with lotus seeds, dried longan, mushrooms and coconut water. Bếp Việt edits the portions for a family meal and specifies that the herbal mix must be food-grade; this dish is not a substitute for medical advice.
ga-ac-tiem-thuoc-bac.finished_dish: The silkie chicken is tender yet holds its shape, with a gently fragrant broth, soft lotus seeds and mild sweetness from the dried longan.
ga-ac-tiem-thuoc-bac.serving: Serve hot in small covered pots with watercress or steamed rice. Offer lime-pepper salt separately if desired.
tips: Choose a clearly labeled food-grade cooking-herb mix and follow its package directions; do not use an unidentified herbal packet.
Soak and rinse dried ingredients. Fresh lotus seeds cook faster, so check their tenderness early.
Do not treat this dish as a remedy or as a replacement for professional health advice.

ga-ac-tiem-thuoc-bac.time_note: About 140 minutes including preparation and soaking; steaming time varies with the chicken and pot size.

ingredients.notes: Soak until tender and remove any bitter germ.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper

preparation_steps: Rinse the chickens, rub lightly with crushed ginger and rice wine, rinse again and drain. Marinate with fish sauce and a little pepper for about 15 minutes.
Soak, rinse and prepare the herbal sachet according to its label. Soak the lotus seeds, dried longan and shiitake mushrooms until tender.
Divide the chicken and dried ingredients between two heatproof covered pots. Mix coconut water with water and salt, then pour it almost to the top of the chicken.
cooking_steps: Set the pots in a steamer over boiling water and cover. Reduce the heat so the water simmers gently.
Steam for about 80–90 minutes until the meat is tender and fully cooked. Add hot water to the steamer if its water level gets low.
Taste and adjust the broth. Serve hot with watercress and a little pepper; this meal is not a medical treatment.

chim-cut-nuong-sa-te.name: Grilled Quail with Vietnamese Satay
chim-cut-nuong-sa-te.description: Quails are marinated with Vietnamese satay, lemongrass, garlic and five-spice, then grilled until golden and fragrant. Bếp Việt balances the seasoning for a family meal; adjust the heat to suit the satay paste.
chim-cut-nuong-sa-te.finished_dish: The skin is golden brown and aromatic with lemongrass, garlic and satay; the meat is fully cooked, tender and savory.
chim-cut-nuong-sa-te.serving: Serve hot with lettuce, cucumber and steamed rice; offer extra chili sauce separately.
tips: Pat the quails dry so the marinade adheres. Marinate under refrigeration and do not leave raw poultry at room temperature for long.
For oven cooking, preheat and turn the quails halfway through; cooking time varies with their size.
Do not use raw-poultry marinade as a dipping sauce. Check that the meat is fully cooked before serving.

chim-cut-nuong-sa-te.time_note: About 110 minutes including chilled marinating; oven or charcoal cooking times vary with the equipment.

ingredients.notes: Adjust for the saltiness of the satay.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the savory heat.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil

ingredients.name: Lettuce
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese mint
ingredients.notes: Wash and serve alongside.

preparation_steps: Rinse the quails, drain and pat dry. Mix the satay, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, ginger, five-spice, fish sauce and sugar into a marinade.
Coat the quails, cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least one hour. Wash hands and utensils after handling raw poultry.
Wash and drain the lettuce and mint, and slice the cucumber. Preheat the oven to 180°C or prepare a grill.
cooking_steps: Arrange the quails on a lined tray or grill rack and lightly brush them with oil.
Grill at 180°C for about 25–30 minutes, turning halfway through. Over charcoal, cook over medium heat and turn regularly to prevent scorching.
Check that the quails are fully cooked, with no raw meat near the joints. Rest for a few minutes and serve with the vegetables.

chim-cau-ham-hat-sen-com.name: Pigeon Stew with Lotus Seeds and Young Green Rice
aliases: Pigeon with lotus seeds and cốm
Stuffed pigeon with lotus seeds and green rice
chim-cau-ham-hat-sen-com.serving_basis: One pigeon cut into four portions for a small family feast.
chim-cau-ham-hat-sen-com.description: A pigeon is filled with young green rice, lotus seeds, minced pork and shiitake mushrooms, then gently stewed in stock. The dish is recorded as part of Hanoi’s traditional Tết banquet; Bếp Việt adapts the portions for four and keeps the filling moderate so the bird cooks evenly.
chim-cau-ham-hat-sen-com.finished_dish: The pigeon meat is tender, with a soft, nutty filling scented by young green rice; the broth has a gentle savory sweetness from the bird, mushrooms and lotus seeds.
chim-cau-ham-hat-sen-com.serving: Cut the pigeon into portions, spoon over some broth and finish with cilantro and pepper. Serve hot with steamed rice or as part of a festive meal.
tips: Do not overfill the cavity; leave room for the filling to expand and cook evenly.
Par-cook the lotus seeds and simmer gently, skimming the broth for a clear finish.
Cook the pigeon fully. Thaw frozen poultry in the refrigerator before preparation.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper

preparation_steps: Rinse the pigeon, rub briefly with salt and a little rice wine and ginger, rinse again and drain. Season the minced pork lightly with fish sauce, salt and pepper.
Par-cook the lotus seeds and divide them. Soak the mushrooms and noodles; mince some mushrooms, cut the noodles short and mince the shallots.
Mix the pork with cốm, half the lotus seeds, minced mushrooms, a little noodle and shallot. Fill the cavity moderately and secure it with kitchen twine or a food-safe skewer.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and lightly brown the pigeon on all sides over medium heat; it does not need to cook through at this stage.
Place it in a pot with hot stock, ginger and strained mushroom soaking liquid. Bring to a boil, skim, then cover and simmer gently for about 35–40 minutes.
Add the remaining lotus seeds and mushrooms and simmer for five minutes. Add the noodles and cook until just tender; season the broth and check the pigeon is fully cooked.
Remove the pigeon, cut into portions and serve with the broth. Finish with pepper and cilantro.

ga-ta-bo-xoi.name: Free-Range Chicken Wrapped in Sticky Rice
ga-ta-bo-xoi.serving_basis: One whole chicken wrapped in sticky rice, cut into about six portions.
ga-ta-bo-xoi.description: Free-range chicken is seasoned and filled with lotus seeds and mushrooms, then roasted before being fully wrapped in steamed sticky rice. The rice is fried until crisp around the tender chicken. This is a make-ahead celebration dish; Bếp Việt reorganizes the steps for home cooking.
ga-ta-bo-xoi.finished_dish: A crisp golden rice shell encloses the whole chicken; the meat inside is tender and the lotus-seed and mushroom filling is fragrant and nutty.
ga-ta-bo-xoi.serving: Rest briefly, then cut through the rice shell and chicken into portions. Serve with pickled vegetables, fresh herbs and dipping sauce on the side.
tips: Soak the glutinous rice fully and drain it well before steaming; overly wet rice is difficult to wrap and may splatter in hot oil.
Let the chicken cool slightly before wrapping. Spread the rice evenly, neither too thick nor too thin, for an even crust.
Use a deep pot with enough oil and do not overcrowd it. Ensure the chicken is cooked through before wrapping and keep raw-poultry preparation separate.

ingredients.name: Pickled vegetables

preparation_steps: Rinse and soak the glutinous rice in water for 7–8 hours, then rinse and drain thoroughly. Prepare the chicken separately from other ingredients; rinse and pat it dry.
Rehydrate the shiitake and wood ear mushrooms, rinse and chop. Steam or simmer the lotus seeds until nearly tender; mince the shallots and slice the ginger and lime leaves.

Marinate the chicken with some fish sauce, salt, pepper and oyster sauce for about 30 minutes. Sauté the shallots, mushrooms, lotus seeds, ginger and lime leaves until cooked, then fill the chicken moderately.
Toss the drained rice with the remaining salt and turmeric. Prepare the oven, steamer and a clean wide surface for wrapping.
cooking_steps: Roast the chicken at 200°C for about 55–65 minutes, turning halfway through; check that the meat near the bone is cooked. Remove and let it cool slightly.
Steam the rice for about 30–40 minutes until tender and sticky. Fluff it, then spread it evenly over a clean heat-safe liner.
Place the chicken in the center and wrap it completely, pressing the rice into an even layer that is neither too thick nor too thin. Let the surface dry slightly before frying.
Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Carefully lower in the wrapped chicken and turn until the rice shell is crisp and golden. Drain on a rack, rest briefly, slice and serve hot.
